title: WP-UAT-A: freeze the badf-uat capability contract (G10 business-acceptance router; DESIGNED)
objective: Freeze badf-uat as the G10 BUSINESS-ACCEPTANCE capability: it produces exactly the `uat` G10 evidence type, never `release-packet`, `operational-readiness` (badf-production-readiness) or `go-no-go` (release_authority, human-reserved). The capability resolves the existing PRD->OBJ->AC->REQ traceability chain (schemas/traceability.schema.json's requirement_to_objective and criterion_to_requirement link maps) rather than re-deriving it, and adds the one leaf that chain does not carry: the UAT Scenario (business-readable, adapter-independent). Execution adapters (browser/API/manual/hybrid) are pure observers; none is registered as a subskill at this rung. The whole capability turns on one distinction: technical E2E verification proves the system did not crash; UAT proves the observed behavior satisfies the business outcome an approved acceptance criterion named. Automation establishes observation; final product acceptance is a separate human decision (the two-layer artifact: this skill's recommendation vs. a human's acceptance). DESIGNED rung: SKILL.md + references only.
business_value: G10 names `uat` as a required evidence type with no producing capability (discovered and filed separately as Issue #238 / GOV-0106, not silently folded into this freeze). Without this capability there is no BADF-native way to distinguish a release that technically works from one the business actually accepts, and no structural boundary preventing a technical E2E pass from being mistaken for acceptance. This freezes the model -- an evidence chain from approved intent through to a bounded recommendation, with human acceptance held outside the producing skill -- so later rungs can enforce it deterministically.
